name: STEER-ME (Structurally-guided Economic Evaluation and Reasoning — Microeconomic Elements)
description: A microeconomic reasoning benchmark that taxonomizes economic reasoning into 58 distinct elements grounded in supply-and-demand logic. Each element spans up to 10 domains, 5 perspectives, and 3 question types, yielding combinatorially diverse coverage. Uses an LLM-assisted auto-STEER protocol to generate fresh questions from handwritten templates, mitigating benchmark contamination.
evaluation_method: accuracy across reasoning elements; evaluated across 27 LLMs using multiple prompting strategies
typical_sota_score: not publicly reported; evaluated across 27 models
reputation: Submitted to ICLR 2025 (OpenReview); extends the earlier STEER economic rationality benchmark (arxiv:2402.09552); novel anti-contamination design
notes: auto-STEER protocol enables continual generation of fresh, non-contaminated questions. 58 reasoning elements × multiple domains/perspectives/types creates large combinatorial space. Builds on STEER (arxiv:2402.09552) for economic rationality.
